Alex M: Heads-up — started seeing a p99 tail for tenant acme-ai on shared-gpu-pool-b around 2026-03-17T18:03Z. p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms, throughput down ~30%. Filing here to triage. @perfbot can you dump recent metrics?

perfbot: Summary (last 30m): tenant=acme-ai p50=48ms p95=210ms p99=420ms qps=85 -> 60 (-29%). kernel_switch_rate +180% vs baseline. kv_evictions spike coincident. Links: https://dash.redwood/pool-b/tenants/acme-ai (graphs attached) :eyes:

Priya S: Is this noisy-neighbor or tenant workload change? Any recent deploys for acme-ai?

Alex M: No deploys from acme-ai team. We rolled kernel-autoswitch tweak to pool-b yesterday (rollout tag: kernel-autoswitch-v3). Suspect interaction between autoswitch + batching heuristic + KV behavior.

Mateo R: I pulled selector logs and perf profile. Observations: rapid toggles when sequence length spikes >512 tokens. When we flip to matmul_fallback we see ~3x token latency. Also KV cache shows repeated evictions for acme-ai which forces re-reads and kernel path changes. Snippets:
```
[kernel_selector] 2026-03-17T18:02:57Z tenant=acme-ai seq_len=1024 selected=matmul_fallback reason=kv_pressure
[kernel_selector] 2026-03-17T18:03:01Z tenant=acme-ai seq_len=18 selected=flash_attn_v2 reason=batch_small
[kv_cache] 2026-03-17T18:03:02Z tenant=acme-ai evict_slots=16 used=874MB limit=1GB
[kernel_switch] rate=6/min pool=shared-gpu-pool-b
```

Claire D: I sampled batching stats from pool-b. We altered batching_window_ms as part of v3 to reduce latency in general, but for mixed seq workloads it increases variance. Batch histogram (recent): 1-8 tokens: 62%, 9-256: 28%, >256: 10%. Those >256 are causing large batches that overflow pinned KV and trigger kernel fallback.

Priya S: So a long-tail of large contexts from acme-ai + tighter batching window -> occasional big batches -> KV slot pressure -> kernel flip -> tail. Makes sense. Can we mitigate without reverting autoswitch?

Mateo R: Quick mitigations I prototyped locally: 1) tenant-level kernel pin for acme-ai to force flash_attn_v2 for seq<=2048 2) increase tenant.max_kv_pinned from 256MB -> 512MB 3) tweak batching_window_ms to 12ms for pool-b to reduce accidental large batching. Suggested config snippet for canary: 
```
tenant_overrides:
  acme-ai:
    kernel_pin: flash_attn_v2
    max_kv_pinned: 536870912  # bytes
pool_overrides:
  shared-gpu-pool-b:
    batching_window_ms: 12
```

infra-bot: Will create canary rollout for pool-b with tag fix/acme-kv-pin. Canary target: 10% of hosts in pool-b starting in 5m, auto-rollback if p99 > 300ms for 3 consecutive minutes.

Judy L: I can own the canary launch and monitoring. I'll watch p50/p95/p99, kernel_switch_rate, kv_evictions, and qps. If good, we can roll to 100% and then consider a global autoswitch tweak.

Alex M: Action items: Mateo to prepare config PR with tests (kv eviction unit + kernel pin test), Judy to run canary, Claire to run synthetic mixed-seq load to reproduce and add a regression test to perf-suite. PRs: please link here.

Priya S: Also add a short-term alert: kernel_switch_rate > 3/min && kv_evictions > 50 in 5m -> P1 paging to eng-runtime oncall.

Mateo R: I'll open PR #4782 with unit tests and a canary plan. Repro script: `scripts/repro/mixed_seq_kv_stress.sh --tenant acme-ai --qps 100 --seq-dist '[1:8:62,9:256:28,257:2048:10]'`

Judy L: Canary started (hostset 10%). Initial telemetry: p99 -> 260ms (improved), kernel_switch_rate -70%, kv_evictions -60%. Monitoring for 10m then escalate. :+1:

Alex M: Thanks everyone. If canary keeps improving we'll adopt tenant-level pin as a short-term mitigation while we iterate on autoswitch heuristics (make it KV-aware). Follow-up: schedule a design sync tomorrow to discuss adding kv_pressure to kernel selector scoring. :shipit:
